title: NationalState
description: Everything about a nation that is not a ship. The snapshot carries all of it, which is why the scenario format is also the save format. This block is the answer to the project's largest standing schema gap: before it existed, a nation's whole industrial position was one scalar called budget_index.

budget_index.description: Relative naval budget, 100 = RN 1922 baseline. Kept for continuity with the 1922 seed; the blocks below are what actually constrain a build.

construction.description: The build envelope and where the nation sits on its own learning curve. A curve position is per design LINE, not per nation: a yard that has built thirty identical cruisers is not the same yard for a carrier.

envelope_t_equiv_yr.description: A NUMBER where the envelope is flat, AN OBJECT OF year -> t-equiv WHERE IT IS A RAMP. Japan's and Britain's are flat; Germany's goes from 5,600 a year to 104,000 in eight years and forcing it into a scalar would hide the only interesting thing about it.

premium.description: Cost per ton relative to history. 1.00 = no dividend realized yet.

learning_curve.description: Unit-cost multiplier per doubling of cumulative output, e.g. 0.80.

line.description: Design line, e.g. 'CL' or a class id.

opened.description: Year the line opened. A line cannot be ahead of its own opening.

block_capable_yards.description: Yards able to build in prefabricated blocks — the constraint on how fast a conversion kit can be applied.

fuel.description: The shared constraint all four divergences lean on and none of them modeled before. Britain runs a war reserve in months; Japan is fed entirely on imported inputs; Germany's whole thesis is attacking somebody else's imports; only America is self-supplied. A fuel model with no hotel-load term does not work at both ends of the fleet (an Iowa returns 1,092 g/shp-h at 12 kt against a destroyer's ~730), so consumption is authored per class rather than solved from one constant.

reserve_tons.description: Keyed by stream: diesel, oil, avgas, coal.

interdictable.description: Whether an opponent's commerce war can reach it. This flag is where the German thesis becomes arithmetic.

streams.description: Distinct fuel streams the navy must supply. A fleet that runs one distillate for ships, aircraft and jets has a materially shorter logistics tail than one running four.

rating.description: Rating class: seaman, artificer, aircrew, sonar, radar, torpedo.

schools.description: A navy with one school per system rather than one per hull type is buying transferability, and the pool sizes should show it.

stockpiles.description: Keyed by item: torpedoes, shells, mines, depth charges, airframes, engines. Depth rather than variety is a strategy, and it is legible here.

throughput.description: Annual production rates by item — the pipeline behind the stockpile.

infrastructure.description: Docks, locks and anchorages with their real limits. A lock's usable beam has ended more design programs than any admiral.

politics.description: Faction state. Some nations have a second clock inside the same year — an administration whose term ends on a fixed date while the naval program runs on its own schedule.

clocks.description: Dated political events the naval program is downstream of.

deception.description: What this nation is concealing and how. Deception-independence is a design law: four lies with no shared failure mode, which is why they never cascaded. A leak is modeled as arriving and being FILED rather than funded.

independent.description: true = this lie shares no failure mode with any other nation's. This frame has no mutual-hostage mechanism.
